description:
FILED s1061 (Opus, 2026-09-07) from #1061's CPAN-board bisects.  TWO
independent faults land on one board row, and the second hides the first.

FAULT 1 -- TIME.  Under PCL the file takes ~150 s (measured 149.95 s wall on
a loaded box, and it is not a hang: it runs to completion).  Real perl 5.40.3
runs it in well under a second and prints 96/96.  The board's per-file
timeout is 120 s, so `tools/cpan-scoreboard.pl` records
`Text-Balanced-2.07-0  05_extmul.t  FAIL 0 0 124` -- zero rows, the FAIL rule
being "zero ok".  That is why the row reads catastrophic while the file is
merely slow.  (The perl-suite runner has a registered-allowance mechanism for
exactly this, `baselines/perl-suite-timeouts.tsv`; the CPAN board has none.
Giving the board one is a candidate piece of #1502/#1504.)

FAULT 2 -- ROWS.  Given 400 s it finishes and produces 30 rows:
`pass=16 fail=14`.  The s378 board snapshot (`5d941618`) has it at
`PARTIAL 63 33` -- 96 rows, which is perl's full plan.  So 66 rows have gone
missing on top of the slowdown, and the file is stopping early.

REPRODUCE both:
    /usr/bin/time -f 'WALL %e' timeout 400 \
      perl tools/run-dist-t.pl --summary ~/.cpan/build/Text-Balanced-2.07-0 t/05_extmul.t
    cd ~/.cpan/build/Text-Balanced-2.07-0 && perl -Ilib t/05_extmul.t   # 96/0

NOT BISECTED, and the reason is worth writing down rather than retrying
blind: the file's verdict is not stable enough to bisect on a shared box.
Two runs of the SAME tree (`d00bb576`) gave `ok=16 notok=14 rc=0` and
`ok=0 notok=0 rc=0`; at a 240 s step timeout, load alone flips a step between
"16/14" and "timeout", and at 600 s a ten-step bisect costs up to an hour of
exclusive box.  Do it on a quiet machine with `--rtimeout 600`
(scratch/s1061/bisect.pl in this session's worktree is the driver), or first
fix FAULT 1 so a step is seconds instead of minutes -- the profile is the
cheaper question and probably answers both, since a 150 s file that loses its
tail smells like one pathological loop.

Text-Balanced is the board's biggest single holder of failing rows (300 of
635 at the s344 survey, docs/cpan-board14-partials-s344.md family B), so this
file is worth the profile.

=== FAULT 1 FIXED, FAULT 2 PROFILED (s473w, 2026-09-09) ===

FAULT 1 (TIME) IS ANSWERED AS AN INSTRUMENT PROBLEM, which is what it was:
`baselines/cpan-board-timeouts.tsv` (task #1502) gives the file 400 s, so the
board no longer records `FAIL 0 0 124` with no rows at all.  It reads
**PARTIAL 16/14** and its 30 rows are visible for the first time since the
s378 snapshot.  The allowance is registered with its measurement and its cause,
and the allowances in effect are announced on every board run.

FAULT 2 (ROWS) IS UNTOUCHED â 30 rows where perl produces 96 â and its cause is
now named: **#1568**, `Text::Balanced::extract_quotelike` and `extract_tagged`
return UNDEF where perl extracts.  Every failing row of the four Text-Balanced
files is that, and 05_extmul.t's 14 are unnamed rows (one #1041 key).

=== PROFILED (s473w) â and what the profile says is "no single statement" ===

THE SPLIT.  Transpile 0.88 s; the SBCL side ~150-190 s.  So the time is all on
the run side, not the compiler (the #184 lesson applied first).

THE FORM-BY-FORM MEASUREMENT, which is the one that worked: a harness that
`read`s the emitted file and `eval`s it ONE TOP-LEVEL FORM AT A TIME, timing
each (scratch `formtime.lisp`; ~860 forms).  Whole run 3m09 (including ~40 s of
runtime load), and **exactly TWO forms exceeded 200 ms**:

    SLOW form 43: 467 ms   (p-eval-always â¦)      \ the `use Text::Balanced`
    SLOW form 44: 4935 ms  (p-eval-always â¦)      / module load

i.e. ~145 s is spread across the remaining ~860 statements at roughly 170 ms
each â just under the threshold, which is why none was reported.  **The file is
not one pathological loop (the guess in this task); it is uniformly slow, ~170
ms per top-level statement**, and every statement of 05_extmul.t is one or two
`extract_multiple` / `extract_quotelike` calls.  So the cost is PER CALL into
Text::Balanced, and the next question is which runtime primitive that module's
inner loop leans on â its `_match_quotelike` drives `/\Gâ¦/gc` over a string
with `pos`, which is the shape #477 already measures as QUADRATIC in PCL.

WHAT DID NOT WORK, recorded so it is not repeated:
  * `sb-sprof` :mode :cpu EXHAUSTED THE HEAP TWICE â 5 ms / 200k samples in a
    4 GB dynamic space, then 20 ms / 30k samples in 8 GB.  Both died in
    "Heap exhausted during garbage collection" before the program finished.
  * timestamping the TAP through a pipe told nothing: SBCL block-buffers
    stdout, so all 30 rows arrive at t=161 s.
  * a second harness that printed the top 20 forms by time exhausted the heap
    for a reason of its own â it called `(format nil "~S" form)` on EVERY form
    to keep a 110-char prefix, which is gigabytes of string over 860 large
    forms.  Keep the prefix only for the forms that cross the threshold.

NEXT STEP, if the per-call cost is worth chasing: lower the threshold to 50 ms
in that harness (without formatting every form) to confirm the flat
distribution, then time ONE `extract_quotelike` call on a 30-character string
against perl â if it is milliseconds against microseconds, this is #477's
family and not a Text::Balanced problem at all.


=== THE ZERO-ROW VERDICT HAS A MECHANISM (s490, Fable, 2026-09-18, main 67781634) ===
The "two runs of the SAME tree gave 16/14 and 0/0 rc=0" instability is not load: the 0/0 run DIES of `Heap exhausted during garbage collection: 0 bytes available` at 1,071,157,824 of 1,073,741,824 bytes (SBCL's default 1 GB dynamic space; *GC-INHIBIT* true at the time), ~100 s in, backtrace top `PCL::%P-REGEX-PARTS` under five levels of the file's own lambdas.  rc is 0 because SBCL's "game over" path is not an exit status the runner reads.  Today it is 0/0 on the board run AND alone with --timeout 300, i.e. the file now sits just ABOVE the limit where at s473w it sat just below.  Output kept: the s490 session scratchpad `extmul.out` (165 lines) -- reproduce with `tools/run-dist-t.pl ~/.cpan/build/Text-Balanced-2.07-0 t/05_extmul.t`.  So FAULT 2's profile should measure ALLOCATION first (bytes consed per statement; is a compiled-scanner or a regex-parts result retained per call?), and the board needs a heap allowance mechanism beside cpan-board-timeouts.tsv.  Owner of the re-bless: #1913.

=== DONE (s513a, Opus 5.5, 2026-10-08) ===
Both faults were one: the `$`-prototype copy of #2860 made extract_multiple loop (rows lost to the heap) and spend ~150 s doing it.  On the s513a tree the file runs to its plan in 14 s: 94 ok / 2 not ok of 96 (perl 96/0); rows 87 + 96 are #2900.  Its 400 s allowance in baselines/cpan-board-timeouts.tsv is DELETED (the registry's own rule: a file that gets faster loses its row); board baselines edited by hand.
subject: Text-Balanced t/05_extmul.t: 96 rows -> 30 (63/33 at the s378 board snapshot, 16/14 now, perl 96/0) AND it needs ~150 s, so the board's 120 s timeout reports it as FAIL 0/0 rc 124 -- two independent faults in one row
